text: The air in the Rusty Anchor was thick with the scent of salt, stale beer, and something vaguely floral that he suspected was trying, and failing, to mask the general funk of a waterfront dive bar in a small Caribbean port.
Jalen Creed sat nursing a weak rum and coke, the condensation on the glass doing little to cool the simmering unease within him.
Outside, the night hummed with the chirping of unseen insects and the rhythmic slosh of waves against the pilings.
Inside, the murmur of conversations in a mix of English and Creole, punctuated by the occasional burst of laughter, painted a familiar backdrop to his solitude.
He was just passing through, another face in the transient tapestry of sailors, traders, and dreamers that drifted in and out of these islands.
A weathered man with a salt-and-pepper beard and eyes that had seen too many sunrises slid onto the stool beside him.
He introduced himself as Mateo, a local who claimed to know the currents and moods of the Caribbean Sea better than his own wife.
Mateo chuckled, a dry, rattling sound.
He gestured with his glass towards the open doorway, where the first hint of a bruised twilight was fading into darkness.
